title: What does IATF 16949 require for competence, training and internal auditor qualification?
description: IATF 16949:2016 clause 7.2 and 7.3 competence and awareness, sanctioned interpretations on training and auditors, and Revision 2 status, November 2026.
shortAnswer: IATF 16949:2016, the International Automotive Task Force (IATF) quality management standard for automotive production and service parts, adds supplemental competence requirements to ISO 9001. Organizations need a documented process for identifying training needs, including awareness, for everyone whose work affects product and process conformity; on-the-job training for new or changed responsibilities; and a documented process verifying internal auditor competence against minimum criteria. As at November 2026, IATF plans to publish Revision 2 in mid-2027.
keyTakeaways: Clause 7.2.1, as amended by Sanctioned Interpretation 22 (effective November 2021), requires a documented process for identifying training needs, including awareness, and for achieving competence of all personnel affecting conformity to product and process requirements.
Training and awareness must also cover prevention information such as recognizing symptoms of pending equipment failure and attempted cyber-attacks.

Clause 7.2.3, as revised by Sanctioned Interpretation 4 (effective September 2020), sets five minimum competencies for internal auditors, plus extra technical requirements for manufacturing process and product auditors and trainer competence evidence.
IATF has said there is no single industry training that covers product safety, because requirements depend on customer and regulatory requirements for each part.
IATF's July 2026 communiqué gives mid-2027 as the planned publication of IATF 16949 Revision 2, with transition ending in line with the ISO 9001 transition.
regulator: No regulator: the International Automotive Task Force (IATF) owns the standard; certification is by IATF-recognized certification bodies
appliesTo: Organizations manufacturing automotive production parts, service parts or accessory parts that seek or hold IATF 16949 certification
Personnel performing activities that affect conformity to product and process requirements
Internal quality management system, manufacturing process and product auditors, and those who train them
Second-party auditors who audit the organization's suppliers

sections.heading: What is IATF 16949 and how does it relate to ISO 9001?

blocks.text: IATF 16949:2016 is the automotive sector's quality management system standard, and it is used together with ISO 9001 rather than instead of it. The IATF states in its [published FAQs](https://www.iatfglobaloversight.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/IATF-16949-FAQs_June-2026.pdf) that the 1st edition was published in October 2016.

Clause numbers follow ISO 9001. Where ISO 9001 clause 7.2 sets the general competence duty and 7.3 sets awareness, IATF 16949 adds numbered supplements such as 7.2.1 to 7.2.4 and 7.3.1. The full text is a purchased document and is not reproduced here. The IATF publishes two kinds of public clarification: Sanctioned Interpretations (SIs), which change how a requirement must be applied, and Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs), which explain existing requirements. For the ISO 9001 base requirements, see [ISO 9001 competence requirements](/regulations/iso-9001-competence-requirements).

sections.heading: What does clause 7.2.1 require for identifying training needs?

blocks.text: Clause 7.2.1 requires a documented process for identifying training needs and achieving competence across the workforce that affects quality. The current wording comes from [Sanctioned Interpretation 22](https://www.iatfglobaloversight.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/IATF-16949-SIs-Nov-2025.pdf), issued in July 2021 and effective November 2021:

blocks.title: IATF 16949 clause 7.2.1 as amended by SI 22
blocks.text: "The organization shall establish and maintain a documented process(es) for identifying training needs including awareness (see Section 7.3.1) and achieving competence of all personnel performing activities affecting conformity to product and process requirements. Personnel performing specific assigned tasks shall be qualified, as required, with particular attention to the satisfaction of customer requirements."

SI 22 added a further sentence: to reduce or eliminate risks to the organization, training and awareness must also include information about prevention relevant to the organization's working environments and employees' responsibilities, "such as recognizing the symptoms of pending equipment failure and/or attempted cyber-attacks." The same set of SIs added cyber-attack threats to the risk analysis in clause 6.1.2.1 (SI 21), so cyber awareness for plant staff is now an explicit audit topic rather than an IT matter alone.

Two features distinguish this from ISO 9001. The process must be documented, and it explicitly links training needs to awareness under 7.3.1, so awareness cannot be handled as an informal communication exercise separate from the training system.

sections.heading: What on-the-job training does IATF 16949 expect?

blocks.text: Clause 7.2.2 requires on-the-job training for personnel with new or modified responsibilities affecting conformity. Public summaries, such as [Advisera's explanation of IATF 16949 competence](https://advisera.com/16949academy/blog/2017/10/04/how-to-ensure-competence-of-your-employees-according-to-iatf-16949/), describe the requirement as covering quality, internal and legislative requirements, scaled to the person's education and the complexity of the task, and including informing people whose work can affect quality about the consequences of nonconformity to customer requirements.

In practice this means a job change, a new product launch or a changed work instruction should create an on-the-job training record for the people affected, and the content should show the customer impact of getting the task wrong. A [skills matrix](/glossary/skills-matrix) that lists operations by workstation is the usual way auditors test this at the line.

sections.heading: What competence must IATF 16949 internal auditors demonstrate?

blocks.text: Clause 7.2.3, as revised by Sanctioned Interpretation 4 (reissued August 2020, effective September 2020), requires a documented process to verify that internal auditors are competent, taking into account organization and customer-specific requirements, with ISO 19011 referenced for guidance. The organization must maintain a list of qualified internal auditors.
Quality management system auditors, manufacturing process auditors and product auditors must all be able to demonstrate these minimum competencies:

items: Understanding of the automotive process approach for auditing, including risk-based thinking.
Understanding of applicable ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 requirements related to the scope of the audit.
Understanding of applicable core tool requirements related to the scope of the audit.
Understanding how to plan, conduct, report and close out audit findings.

blocks.text: Manufacturing process auditors must additionally demonstrate technical understanding of the processes audited, including process risk analysis such as PFMEA and the control plan. Product auditors must demonstrate competence in product requirements and the use of relevant measuring and test equipment. Where the organization's own personnel provide the auditor training, documented information must show the trainer's competence against these requirements. SI 4 also notes that the clause's items f) and g) still apply; [Advisera's summary of internal auditor competence](https://advisera.com/16949academy/blog/2017/10/19/requirements-for-competence-of-iatf-16949-internal-auditors/) describes these as conducting a minimum number of audits per year set by the organization and maintaining knowledge of internal and external changes.

sections.heading: What about second-party auditors and awareness under clause 7.3?

blocks.text: IATF 16949 also sets competence requirements for second-party auditors (clause 7.2.4), meaning the organization's people who audit its suppliers, and adds supplemental awareness requirements in clause 7.3.1. Neither clause is the subject of a current Sanctioned Interpretation, so the purchased standard is the authority on their exact wording.

The practical link is the one SI 22 makes explicit: awareness needs are identified through the same documented training needs process as competence. Organizations should therefore show, for each role, what employees must be aware of about their impact on product quality and customer requirements, and how that awareness is checked, alongside their competence records.

sections.heading: Is there a required product safety training course?

blocks.text: No single course is prescribed. In FAQ 13 on product safety (clause 4.4.1.2), the IATF says the people assigned to tasks must be competent, that competence includes the rules and regulations associated with the task, and that "there is no single complete industry training on this topic." Organizations must review customer and regulatory requirements for each part and its intended country of use, and some customers specify product safety training, knowledge and personnel requirements.

For a training manager, that turns product safety into a mapping exercise: each element of 4.4.1.2 becomes a competence requirement assigned to the roles that perform it, such as engineers developing PFMEAs and control plans for safety-related characteristics.

In [Stakeholder Communiqué SC-2024-006](https://www.iatfglobaloversight.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/IATF-Stakeholder-Communique-SC-2024-006-IATF-16949-Revision-2.pdf) (October 2024), the IATF announced it had started revising IATF 16949:2016 and expected the new version after publication of the revised ISO 9001. [SC-2026-005](https://www.iatfglobaloversight.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Stakeholder-Communique-SC-2026-005_IATF-16949-2nd-Edition-status.pdf) (July 2026) set out five priorities: simplification and clarity, software quality assurance, Tier N supply chain management, launch management, and customer-specific requirements.

The July 2026 timeline is indicative: working draft and external feedback in 2026, final validation and translation in 2027, planned publication in mid-2027, and an end of transition aligned with the end of the ISO 9001 transition. As at November 2026, IATF 16949:2016 and its Sanctioned Interpretations remain the basis for certification.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry represents the competence requirements of each role, including customer-specific requirements and core tools, as a framework of concepts and assessment points before any course is written. The internal auditor criteria in SI 4 become a reusable competence profile, and changes such as a new Sanctioned Interpretation can be traced to the roles and records they affect.

faqs.q: Does IATF 16949 require a documented training procedure?
faqs.a: Yes. Clause 7.2.1, as amended by Sanctioned Interpretation 22, requires the organization to establish and maintain a documented process for identifying training needs, including awareness, and achieving competence of all personnel performing activities affecting conformity to product and process requirements.

faqs.q: Do IATF 16949 internal auditors need an external certificate?
faqs.a: Clause 7.2.3 does not require an external certificate. It requires a documented process to verify competence against minimum criteria and a list of qualified auditors. If internal staff train the auditors, the organization must retain evidence of the trainer's competence. Some customer-specific requirements may set additional expectations.

faqs.q: Does cyber security awareness apply to production staff under IATF 16949?
faqs.a: Yes, where relevant to their working environment. Sanctioned Interpretation 22 added to clause 7.2.1 that training and awareness should include prevention information such as recognizing symptoms of pending equipment failure and attempted cyber-attacks, effective November 2021.

faqs.q: When will the new edition of IATF 16949 be published?
faqs.a: The IATF's July 2026 communiqué gives mid-2027 as the planned publication date for Revision 2, with dates described as indicative. The end of the transition period is to be aligned with the end of the ISO 9001 transition.
